recommendation_summary: Act now: keep the spreadsheet as the booking record, but send every new booking through one save step, a Google Apps Script web form. That step takes a LockService lock, checks the item's dates for overlap, then either appends the row or rejects the booking. Agents lose direct edit access so nobody can bypass it. Optional: conditional formatting may stay as a warning only, not as the control. Unmet: the reply doesn't know which spreadsheet product the user runs, and for Excel it gives no equivalent locking design or date.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The owner requires that a conflicting reservation be rejected at save time, even when two agents submit at the same moment. You want something shippable this week.
labels.Deleted: Relying on agents noticing red cells and remembering to check them, since that is the human process that already failed last week.
labels.Bottleneck: Nothing stops a save. Six agents in two offices can each check, see no conflict, and both save.
labels.Checked myself: Only what you told me: one identifier per item, six concurrent agents, last week's double booking, and the owner's save-time rule. I haven't seen the spreadsheet or which product it runs on.

note: The reply picks a locked, server-side check-then-append step with direct edits removed, so of two simultaneous conflicting bookings only one is saved, and formatting is demoted to a warning.
